properties.name: Zeus
properties.description: King of the Olympian gods, ruler of Mount Olympus, and god of sky and thunder. Known for his affairs that produced demigods.

properties.name: Athena
properties.description: Goddess of wisdom, strategic warfare, and crafts. Born fully armored from Zeus's head. Patron of Athens, protector of heroes.

properties.name: Poseidon
properties.description: God of the sea, earthquakes, and horses. Brother of Zeus. His anger caused storms and earthquakes. Creator of horses.

properties.name: Hades
properties.description: God of the underworld and the dead. Not evil but stern and just. Abducted Persephone. Rich from underground metals and gems.

properties.name: Apollo
properties.description: God of sun, music, poetry, prophecy, and healing. Twin brother of Artemis. Leader of the Muses. Oracle at Delphi was his.

properties.name: Ares
properties.description: God of war and violence, unpopular among gods and mortals. Lover of Aphrodite. Represented the brutal aspect of warfare.

properties.name: Aphrodite
properties.description: Goddess of love, beauty, and desire. Born from sea foam. Her powers could overwhelm gods and mortals alike. Started the Trojan War.

properties.name: Hermes
properties.description: Messenger of the gods, guide of souls to the underworld. Patron of travelers, thieves, and merchants. Invented the lyre on his first day.

properties.name: Jupiter
properties.description: King of Roman gods, supreme deity of the state religion. Protector of Rome and guarantor of law and social order.

properties.name: Mars
properties.description: Father of Romulus and Remus, second only to Jupiter. Unlike Greek Ares, Mars was respected as guardian of Rome and agriculture.

properties.name: Odin
properties.description: Allfather of the Norse gods. Sacrificed an eye at Mimir's well for wisdom and hung on Yggdrasil for nine days to gain the runes.

properties.name: Thor
properties.description: God of thunder, protector of humanity and the gods. Wielded MjÃ¶lnir, the hammer. Strongest of the Aesir. Fated to die fighting JÃ¶rmungandr.

properties.name: Loki
properties.description: The trickster god, blood-brother of Odin. Shape-shifter who caused mischief ranging from amusing to catastrophic. Father of Fenrir, Hel, and JÃ¶rmungandr.

properties.name: Freyja
properties.description: Vanir goddess of love, fertility, and seiÃ°r magic. Claimed half of battle-slain for her hall FÃ³lkvangr. Most beautiful of the goddesses. Wept golden tears.

properties.name: Ra
properties.description: Supreme sun god of Egypt. Sailed across the sky by day and through the underworld by night. All pharaohs were his sons.

properties.name: Osiris
properties.description: God of the afterlife, death, and resurrection. Murdered by Set and resurrected by Isis. Judge of the dead in the Hall of Two Truths.

properties.name: Isis
properties.description: Goddess of magic, motherhood, and wisdom. Reassembled and resurrected Osiris. One of the most worshipped deities in the ancient world.

properties.name: Anubis
properties.description: Jackal-headed god of mummification and the afterlife. Guided souls to judgment and weighed hearts against Ma'at's feather.

properties.name: Marduk
properties.description: Supreme god of Babylon. Slew Tiamat and created the world from her body. Patron deity of Babylon and king of the gods.

properties.name: Ishtar
properties.description: Goddess of love, war, and fertility. Queen of Heaven. Descended to the underworld and returned. Most important Mesopotamian goddess.

properties.name: Enki
properties.description: God of wisdom, freshwater, and magic. Saved humanity from the flood. Cunning and benevolent artificer who often sided with humans.

properties.name: Vishnu
properties.description: The Preserver in the Hindu trinity. Incarnates as avatars whenever dharma declines. Ten avatars include Rama, Krishna, and Buddha.

properties.name: Shiva
properties.description: The Destroyer and Transformer. Meditates on Mount Kailash. Performs the cosmic dance (Tandava). Third eye unleashes destructive fire.

properties.name: Brahma
properties.description: The Creator in the Hindu trinity. Born from Vishnu's navel on a lotus. Created the universe and all living beings. Has four faces.

properties.name: Ganesha
properties.description: Elephant-headed god of beginnings, wisdom, and obstacle removal. Son of Shiva and Parvati. Invoked at the start of every new venture.

properties.name: Hanuman
properties.description: Monkey god of devotion and strength. Son of Vayu (wind). Supreme devotee of Rama. Can change size and fly across oceans.

properties.name: Durga
properties.description: The supreme goddess created from the combined energies of all gods. Rides a lion/tiger. Slayer of the buffalo demon Mahishasura.

properties.name: Amaterasu
properties.description: Sun goddess and supreme deity of the Shinto pantheon. Ancestor of the Japanese imperial family. Her mirror is one of the three imperial regalia.

properties.name: Susanoo
properties.description: God of storms and the sea. Wild and impetuous. Banished from heaven for his behavior. Slew the eight-headed serpent Yamata no Orochi.

properties.name: Quetzalcoatl
properties.description: The Feathered Serpent, god of wind and learning. Created humanity from bones in the underworld. Associated with Venus as the morning star.

properties.name: Huitzilopochtli
properties.description: Aztec war god and patron of Tenochtitlan. Required human blood to move the sun each day. Born fully armed to defend his mother.

properties.name: Perun
properties.description: Supreme god of the Slavic pantheon. Thunder god who battles the serpent Veles in an eternal cosmic struggle. Associated with oak trees.

properties.name: Veles
properties.description: God of the underworld, cattle, and magic. Eternal adversary of Perun. Associated with serpents, wealth, and poetry.

properties.name: Tengri
properties.description: Supreme sky god of the Turkic peoples. Eternal Blue Heaven. Source of all power and destiny. Not depicted in human form.

properties.name: Umay
properties.description: Mother goddess of the Turkic peoples. Protector of children and pregnant women. Embodiment of the creative feminine principle.

properties.name: Ahura Mazda
properties.description: Supreme creator god of Zoroastrianism. Embodiment of truth (asha) and light. Created the world from pure thought.

properties.name: Olodumare
properties.description: Supreme creator deity of Yoruba religion. Distant and transcendent. Acts through orishas (divine intermediaries).

properties.name: Shango
properties.description: Orisha of thunder, fire, and justice. Deified king of Oyo. Wields a double-headed axe. One of the most popular orishas worldwide.

properties.name: Ogun
properties.description: Orisha of iron, war, and technology. Patron of blacksmiths, warriors, and all who use metal tools. Cleared the path from heaven to earth.

properties.name: Yemoja
properties.description: Mother of all orishas. Goddess of the ocean and rivers. Protector of women, especially pregnant women and children.

properties.name: Inti
properties.description: Sun god and supreme deity of the Inca. Ancestor of the Sapa Inca. Source of warmth and agricultural abundance.

properties.name: Pachamama
properties.description: The living earth goddess. She IS the earth â€” conscious and aware. Demands respect and reciprocal offerings. Still actively worshipped.

properties.name: Maui
properties.description: Polynesian trickster demigod. Fished up islands, snared the sun, stole fire, and died trying to win immortality for humanity.

properties.name: Pele
properties.description: Hawaiian goddess of fire and volcanoes. Lives in KÄ«lauea crater. Both creator and destroyer â€” lava forms new land.

properties.name: VÃ¤inÃ¤mÃ¶inen
properties.description: Eternal sage and singer-hero of the Kalevala. Born old. His songs literally shaped reality. Directly inspired Tolkien's Gandalf.

properties.name: Baal
properties.description: Storm god of the Canaanites. Defeated Sea (Yamm) and Death (Mot). Central to Levantine agriculture and kingship.

properties.name: Teshub
properties.description: Storm god and king of the Hittite pantheon. Born from Kumarbi's swallowing of Anu's manhood. Defeated his father in cosmic battle.

properties.name: Tinia
properties.description: Supreme sky and thunder god of the Etruscans. Wielded three thunderbolts of increasing severity. His decisions were read through lightning.

properties.name: Apedemak
properties.description: Lion-headed war god of Kush. Supreme warrior deity unique to Nubian religion. Depicted with three heads or four arms. Worshipped at Naqa and Musawwarat.

properties.name: Aramazd
properties.description: Supreme creator god of the Armenian pantheon. Cognate with Ahura Mazda. Father of all gods. Annual festival at Garni temple.

properties.name: Amirani
properties.description: Georgian Prometheus-figure. Son of a goddess. Stole fire from the gods. Chained to the Caucasus Mountains where an eagle eats his heart.

properties.name: Jade Emperor
properties.description: Supreme ruler of the celestial bureaucracy. Governs heaven and earth. All other gods report to him. Central to Chinese folk religion.

properties.name: Sun Wukong
properties.description: Born from stone, achieved immortality, wreaked havoc in Heaven. Imprisoned under a mountain for 500 years. Redeemed as Xuanzang's protector.

properties.name: NÃ¼wa
properties.description: Creator of humanity from clay. Repaired the broken sky with five-colored stones. Established the institution of marriage.

properties.name: Avalokiteshvara
properties.description: Bodhisattva of infinite compassion. Vowed not to enter nirvana until all beings are free from suffering. Thousand arms to help all.

properties.name: Fenrir
properties.description: Monstrous wolf, son of Loki. Bound by the gods with magical chain Gleipnir. Destined to break free at RagnarÃ¶k and devour Odin.

properties.name: JÃ¶rmungandr
properties.description: World-encircling sea serpent, child of Loki. Biting its own tail around Midgard. Will release at RagnarÃ¶k to fight Thor.

properties.name: Krishna
properties.description: Eighth avatar of Vishnu. Divine child, lover, warrior, and philosopher. Delivered the Bhagavad Gita. Played enchanting flute.

properties.name: Rama
properties.description: Seventh avatar of Vishnu. Ideal king (maryada purushottam). His story is the Ramayana. Embodiment of dharma and righteous rule.

properties.name: Eshu
properties.description: Orisha of crossroads, messenger between humans and the divine. Trickster who tests and challenges. Must be honored first in all rituals.

properties.name: Tezcatlipoca
properties.description: The Smoking Mirror â€” god of night, fate, and conflict. Rival of Quetzalcoatl. All-seeing through his obsidian mirror. Shape-shifter and cosmic antagonist.

properties.name: Orunmila
properties.description: Orisha of wisdom and divination. Witnessed creation and knows all destinies. Gave humanity the Ifa oracle system.

properties.name: Coyote
properties.description: The great trickster of Native American mythology. Both wise and foolish, creator and destroyer. Stole fire for humanity.

properties.name: Raven
properties.description: Trickster creator of the Pacific Northwest. Stole light from the Sky Chief. Shape-shifter. Both cosmic creator and mischievous fool.

properties.name: Viracocha
properties.description: Supreme creator god of the Inca. Rose from Lake Titicaca. Created sun, moon, stars, and humanity. Departed over the Pacific.

properties.name: MÃ¶ngke Tengri
properties.description: The supreme sky deity of Mongolian religion. Grants divine mandate to rulers. Not personified â€” an eternal, abstract cosmic force.

properties.name: Vahagn
properties.description: Armenian war god born from cosmic fire. Dragon-slayer (Vishapakagh). Stole straw from the Milky Way. Cognate with Vedic Vrtrahan.

properties.name: Artemis
properties.description: Virgin goddess of the hunt, moon, and wilderness. Twin sister of Apollo. Protector of young girls and animals.

properties.name: Hephaestus
properties.description: God of the forge and fire. Lame smith who created divine weapons and automata. Husband of Aphrodite. Built the palaces of Olympus.

properties.name: Demeter
properties.description: Goddess of the harvest and agriculture. Her grief over Persephone's abduction caused winter. Central to the Eleusinian Mysteries.

properties.name: Dionysus
properties.description: God of wine, ecstasy, and theater. Born twice â€” once from his mother and once from Zeus's thigh. His cult involved ecstatic ritual.

properties.name: Prometheus
properties.description: Titan who stole fire from the gods and gave it to humanity, enabling civilization. Punished by Zeus â€” chained to a rock where an eagle ate his liver daily.

properties.name: Diana
properties.description: Roman goddess of the hunt and moon. Guardian of the woods. Protector of the lower classes. Her temple at Nemi was one of Rome's most sacred sites.

properties.name: Venus
properties.description: Roman goddess of love and beauty. Mother of Aeneas, ancestor of the Julian family. More dignified than Greek Aphrodite â€” tied to state power.

properties.name: Mercury
properties.description: Roman messenger god and patron of merchants and thieves. More commercially oriented than Greek Hermes. Featured on Roman coinage.

properties.name: Janus
properties.description: Uniquely Roman two-faced god of beginnings and transitions. No Greek equivalent. January named after him. Guarded all doorways and passages.

properties.name: Frigg
properties.description: Queen of the Aesir, wife of Odin. Goddess of marriage and motherhood. She knows all fates but tells none. Friday named after her.

properties.name: Tyr
properties.description: God of law, justice, and honorable warfare. Sacrificed his hand to bind Fenrir. Tuesday named after him. Bravest of the gods.

properties.name: Hel
properties.description: Daughter of Loki, ruler of the realm of the dead (also called Hel). Half alive, half corpse. Received those who died of illness or old age.

properties.name: Thoth
properties.description: Ibis-headed god of wisdom, writing, and magic. Inventor of hieroglyphics. Keeper of divine records. Mediator between cosmic forces.

properties.name: Sekhmet
properties.description: Lion-headed goddess of war and destruction. Her bloodlust nearly destroyed humanity. Also goddess of healing â€” the one who wounds can heal.

properties.name: Set
properties.description: God of chaos, storms, and the desert. Murdered his brother Osiris. Complex deity â€” also protector of Ra against Apophis. Both villain and champion.

properties.name: Hathor
properties.description: Cow-headed goddess of love, beauty, and joy. Gentle aspect of Sekhmet. Welcomed the dead to the afterlife. Nurse of pharaohs.

properties.name: Horus
properties.description: Falcon-headed god of the sky. Son of Osiris and Isis. Avenged his father by defeating Set. Living pharaohs were his embodiment.

properties.name: Enlil
properties.description: King of the gods before Marduk's rise. God of wind, air, and authority. Decreed the great flood. Temple at Nippur was the most sacred in Mesopotamia.

properties.name: Tiamat
properties.description: Primordial salt-water goddess. Mother of the first gods. Raised an army of monsters when her children threatened her. Slain by Marduk â€” her body became heaven and earth.

properties.name: Gilgamesh
properties.description: Semi-divine king of Uruk, two-thirds god. Protagonist of the world's oldest epic. Sought but failed to achieve immortality, finding legacy instead.

properties.name: Parvati
properties.description: Goddess of love, fertility, and devotion. Wife of Shiva. Mother of Ganesha and Kartikeya. Gentle form of Shakti (divine feminine power).

properties.name: Lakshmi
properties.description: Goddess of wealth, fortune, and beauty. Wife of Vishnu. Emerged from the churning of the cosmic ocean. Worshipped during Diwali.

properties.name: Saraswati
properties.description: Goddess of knowledge, music, and the arts. Wife of Brahma. Sits on a white lotus playing the veena. Her blessings are sought before study.

properties.name: Indra
properties.description: King of the Vedic gods. Thunder god who slew the dragon Vritra to release the waters. Most prominent deity in the Rig Veda.

properties.name: Kali
properties.description: Fierce goddess of destruction and time. Dark-skinned, garlanded with skulls. Destroys evil and ego. Dances on Shiva. Liberator of souls.

properties.name: Tsukuyomi
properties.description: Moon god, born from Izanagi's right eye. Banished from Amaterasu's presence for killing the food goddess Uke Mochi. Night exists because of their estrangement.

properties.name: Inari
properties.description: Kami of rice, fertility, and prosperity. Served by fox (kitsune) messengers. One of Japan's most popular deities â€” over 30,000 shrines.

properties.name: Izanagi
properties.description: Creator god who with Izanami formed the Japanese islands. Father of Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo. His purification created the three noble children.

properties.name: Izanami
properties.description: Creator goddess who died giving birth to fire. Became queen of Yomi (underworld). Her decay horrified Izanagi, binding her to death's realm.

properties.name: Tlaloc
properties.description: Rain god who dwelt on mountain peaks. Both benevolent (rain) and destructive (storms, floods). Dead by drowning went to his paradise Tlalocan.

properties.name: Mictlantecuhtli
properties.description: Lord of Mictlan, the underworld. Skeletal figure adorned with eyeball necklace. Ruled the lowest level of the nine-layered underworld with his wife.

properties.name: Ixchel
properties.description: Maya goddess of the moon, medicine, and weaving. Depicted as an old woman with a serpent on her head, pouring water. Patron of midwives.

properties.name: Kukulkan
properties.description: Maya Feathered Serpent deity, counterpart of Aztec Quetzalcoatl. During equinoxes, his shadow serpent descends El Castillo pyramid at ChichÃ©n ItzÃ¡.

properties.name: Svarog
properties.description: Slavic sky-smith god who forged the sun. Father of the sun god Dazhbog and fire god Svarozhich. Created law and civilization through the forge.

properties.name: Mokosh
properties.description: Mother Earth goddess. Protector of women, spinning, and weaving. Last pagan deity worshipped in Eastern Europe. Connected to moisture and fertility.

properties.name: Ilmarinen
properties.description: The Eternal Hammerer, divine smith of the Kalevala. Forged the sky, the Sampo, and a golden bride. Greatest craftsman in Finnish mythology.

properties.name: Louhi
properties.description: Powerful sorceress, mistress of the dark north (Pohjola). Both enemy and necessary partner. Stole the sun and moon. Commanded frost and disease.

properties.name: Anahit
properties.description: Great Lady of Armenia, goddess of fertility, healing, and wisdom. Her golden statue was Armenia's most revered religious object. Cognate with Persian Anahita.

properties.name: Erlik
properties.description: Lord of the underworld in Turkic-Mongol mythology. First being created but fell into evil. Rules the lower world. Shamans must placate him.

properties.name: Angra Mainyu
properties.description: The cosmic adversary of Ahura Mazda. Source of all evil, disease, and death. Will ultimately be defeated at the end of time.

properties.name: Rostam
properties.description: Greatest hero of Persian mythology. Completed seven labors, served multiple kings. Tragically killed his own son Sohrab in combat.

properties.name: Simorgh
properties.description: Benevolent mythical bird nesting atop the World Tree. Raised the hero Zal. Possesses all knowledge accumulated through three cosmic destructions.

properties.name: TÄne Mahuta
properties.description: God of forests and birds. Separated his parents Rangi (Sky) and Papa (Earth) to bring light. Created the first woman from clay.

properties.name: Tangaroa
properties.description: God of the sea throughout Polynesia. Father of fish and reptiles. His domain was the vast Pacific that Polynesian navigators mastered.

properties.name: Rainbow Serpent
properties.description: The great creative spirit of Aboriginal Australian mythology. Shaped the landscape, created rivers and valleys. Enforces law and punishes transgressors.

properties.name: White Buffalo Calf Woman
properties.description: Sacred figure who brought the chanunpa (sacred pipe) and seven sacred rites to the Lakota people. Transformed into a white buffalo calf.

properties.name: Spider Woman
properties.description: Creator and protector in Navajo, Hopi, and other traditions. Taught weaving. Guides heroes through the underworld. Weaves the web of life.

properties.name: Sedna
properties.description: Inuit goddess of the sea. Rules all marine animals from the ocean floor. Shamans must comb her hair to release animals for hunting.

properties.name: Oshun
properties.description: Orisha of the Oshun River, love, fertility, and beauty. Youngest orisha. Her sweetness hides fierce power. One of Shango's wives.

properties.name: Oya
properties.description: Orisha of wind, lightning, and transformation. Guardian of the cemetery gates. Shango's most powerful wife. Fierce warrior goddess.

properties.name: Obatala
properties.description: Father of all orishas, creator of human bodies. Associated with white, purity, and moral clarity. Got drunk on palm wine during creation.

properties.name: CÃº Chulainn
properties.description: Greatest hero of the Ulster Cycle. Son of the god Lugh. His battle frenzy (rÃ­astrad) transformed him into a terrifying creature. Died standing, tied to a pillar.

properties.name: The Dagda
properties.description: Good god of the Tuatha DÃ© Danann. Wielded a club that could kill and resurrect, a cauldron of plenty, and a harp that controlled seasons and emotions.

properties.name: Lugh
properties.description: Master of all arts and skills. Father of CÃº Chulainn. Led the Tuatha DÃ© Danann to victory. Lughnasadh harvest festival named after him.

properties.name: Brigid
properties.description: Triple goddess of fire, poetry, and healing. So beloved she was absorbed into Christianity as St. Brigid. Imbolc (February 1st) is her festival.

properties.name: El
properties.description: Father of the gods in Canaanite religion. Wise and ancient. Presided over the divine council. His name became the Hebrew word for God.

properties.name: Astarte
properties.description: Great goddess of the Phoenicians. Queen of Heaven. Combined love and war aspects. Worshipped across the Mediterranean through Phoenician colonies.

properties.name: Menrva
properties.description: Etruscan goddess of wisdom and war, part of the primary triad with Tinia and Uni. Directly became Roman Minerva. Patroness of artisans and healers.

properties.name: Charun
properties.description: Etruscan demon of death who guarded the underworld entrance. Blue-skinned with a hammer. Not evil but inevitable â€” he guided souls to their destination.

properties.name: Kumarbi
properties.description: Father of the gods in Hurrian-Hittite mythology. Overthrew Anu by biting off his genitals. Father of Teshub. Parallel to Greek Kronos.

properties.name: Baba Yaga
properties.description: Ancient forest witch living in a hut on chicken legs. Both terrifying and helpful. Tests heroes with impossible tasks. Mortar and pestle are her vehicle.

properties.name: Guan Yu
properties.description: Deified historical general from the Three Kingdoms period. God of war, loyalty, and brotherhood. Worshipped by police, triads, and businesses alike.

properties.name: Guanyin
properties.description: Chinese form of Avalokiteshvara. Goddess of mercy and compassion. One of the most worshipped deities in East Asia. Hears all prayers.

properties.name: Mazu
properties.description: Deified mortal who became goddess of the sea and protector of sailors. Over 1,500 temples worldwide. Patron of fishermen and navigators.

properties.name: Mama Quilla
properties.description: Moon goddess, wife of Inti. Protector of married women. Her tears were silver. Lunar eclipses were her being attacked by a cosmic serpent.

properties.name: Siddhartha Gautama (Buddha)
properties.description: The historical Buddha, born a prince. Achieved enlightenment under the Bodhi tree. Not a god but a fully awakened being. Taught the Middle Way.

properties.name: Mara
properties.description: Lord of illusion and death. Tempted the Buddha before enlightenment. Represents the internal obstacles to awakening â€” desire, fear, and ego.

properties.name: Hwanung
properties.description: Son of the Lord of Heaven who descended to Mount Baekdu. Father of Dangun. Brought wind, rain, and cloud ministers. Established laws and taught agriculture.

properties.name: Anansi
properties.description: The Spider trickster of Akan tradition. Owns all stories. Uses wit rather than strength. Traveled to the Americas through the slave trade.

properties.name: Heracles
properties.description: Greatest hero of Greek mythology. Son of Zeus and Alcmene. Completed twelve impossible labors. Achieved immortality through suffering.

properties.name: Achilles
properties.description: Greatest warrior of the Trojan War. Son of Peleus and Thetis. Nearly invulnerable except his heel. Chose glory and short life over obscurity and long life.

properties.name: Odysseus
properties.description: King of Ithaca, cleverest of the Greeks. Conceived the Trojan Horse. Spent ten years returning home. Master of deception and survival.

properties.name: Hera
properties.description: Queen of the Olympian gods, wife of Zeus. Goddess of marriage and childbirth. Known for her jealous rage against Zeus's lovers and their children.

properties.name: Juno
properties.description: Queen of the Roman gods. June named after her. Protector of the state and women. Part of the Capitoline Triad with Jupiter and Minerva.

properties.name: Minerva
properties.description: Roman goddess of wisdom and strategic warfare. Part of the Capitoline Triad. Patron of artisans, doctors, and musicians.

properties.name: Pluto
properties.description: Roman god of the underworld and wealth. Less feared than Hades. Underground riches (metals, gems) were his domain. Abducted Proserpina.

properties.name: Ceres
properties.description: Roman goddess of agriculture and motherly love. Her grief over Proserpina's abduction caused the seasons. Cereal grains named after her.

properties.name: Persephone
properties.description: Queen of the Underworld and goddess of spring. Daughter of Demeter. Her annual return causes spring; her descent brings winter.

properties.name: Pan
properties.description: God of the wild, shepherds, and rustic music. Half-goat, half-man. His shout caused 'panic' in enemies. Played reed pipes in Arcadian mountains.

properties.name: Hecate
properties.description: Triple-formed goddess of magic, crossroads, and the night. Guardian of thresholds. Aided Demeter in searching for Persephone.

properties.name: Balder
properties.description: Most beloved of the Norse gods, son of Odin and Frigg. Beautiful and pure. Killed by mistletoe. His death heralds RagnarÃ¶k.

properties.name: Heimdall
properties.description: Guardian of Bifrost, the rainbow bridge. Born of nine mothers. Can hear grass grow and see for hundreds of miles. Will blow Gjallarhorn at RagnarÃ¶k.

properties.name: NjÃ¶rÃ°r
properties.description: Vanir god of the sea, wind, and wealth. Father of Freyja and Freyr. Patron of sailors and fishermen. Married the giantess Skadi.

properties.name: Freyr
properties.description: Vanir god of fertility, sunshine, and rain. Twin brother of Freyja. Gave up his sword for love. Will be among the first to fall at RagnarÃ¶k.

properties.name: Bastet
properties.description: Cat-headed goddess of home, fertility, and protection. Once fierce (lioness), she became gentle (cat). Her festival at Bubastis was Egypt's largest.

properties.name: Ptah
properties.description: Creator god of Memphis. Created the world through speech and thought (logos). Patron of craftsmen and architects. Father of Nefertem.

properties.name: Ma'at
properties.description: Goddess of truth, justice, and cosmic order. Her feather weighed against the heart of the dead. Without Ma'at, the universe returns to chaos.

properties.name: Ereshkigal
properties.description: Queen of the Underworld. Sister and mirror of Ishtar. Rules the Land of No Return. All who enter her domain are stripped of power.

properties.name: Shamash
properties.description: Sun god and god of justice. Gave laws to Hammurabi. Sees all things from his daily journey across the sky. Twin of Ishtar.

properties.name: Sin
properties.description: Moon god of Ur. Father of Shamash and Ishtar. Drove the crescent moon as a boat across the night sky. Patron of timekeeping.

properties.name: Dangun
properties.description: Legendary founder of Gojoseon (first Korean kingdom, 2333 BCE). Son of Hwanung and a she-bear who became human. National ancestor of all Koreans.

properties.name: Jangseung
properties.description: Guardian spirit embodied in carved wooden poles at village entrances. Male and female pairs protect villages from evil spirits and disease.

properties.name: Eshmun
properties.description: Phoenician god of healing. Died and was resurrected. Major cult center at Sidon. Later identified with Greek Asclepius.

properties.name: Hepat
properties.description: Sun goddess and queen of the gods in Hittite religion. Wife of Teshub. Most important female deity in the Hittite pantheon. Worshipped at Arinna.

properties.name: Vanth
properties.description: Winged female death spirit of Etruscan mythology. Gentle guide of souls â€” unlike terrifying Charun, Vanth comforts the dying. Often depicted with torches.

properties.name: Amun of Napata
properties.description: Nubian version of Amun, centered at Jebel Barkal. Legitimized Kushite kings as true pharaohs. His oracle at Napata influenced politics for centuries.

properties.name: Medea
properties.description: Granddaughter of Helios, divine sorceress of Colchis. In Georgian tradition, a powerful priestess of the sun cult. Her knowledge of plants was unmatched.

properties.name: Yama
properties.description: God of death and justice. First mortal to die, he became ruler of the dead. Rides a buffalo. Weighs deeds with perfect dharmic balance.

properties.name: Agni
properties.description: God of fire and the divine messenger. Present in every sacrificial fire, carrying offerings to the gods. Second most mentioned deity in the Rig Veda after Indra.

properties.name: Surya
properties.description: Sun god who rides a chariot drawn by seven horses across the sky. Father of Yama and the Ashvins. Konark Sun Temple is dedicated to him.

properties.name: Vayu
properties.description: God of wind and breath. Father of Hanuman and Bhima. Represents the life-force (prana). One of the oldest Vedic deities.

properties.name: Sita
properties.description: Wife of Rama, avatar of Lakshmi. Born from the earth. Abducted by Ravana and rescued. Embodiment of wifely devotion and moral purity.

properties.name: Radha
properties.description: Supreme beloved of Krishna. Their love represents the soul's longing for the divine. Not mentioned in early texts but central to later bhakti devotion.

properties.name: Kartikeya
properties.description: God of war and son of Shiva. Six-faced, rides a peacock. Commander of the divine army. Extremely popular in South India as Murugan.

properties.name: FÅ«jin
properties.description: God of wind, depicted carrying a bag of winds on his shoulders. One of the oldest Shinto deities. His companion is Raijin the thunder god.

properties.name: Raijin
properties.description: God of thunder and lightning. Beats his ring of drums to create thunder. Often depicted alongside FÅ«jin at temple gates.

properties.name: Hachiman
properties.description: God of war and divine protector of Japan. Patron of the samurai class. Deified Emperor Ojin. Over 25,000 shrines across Japan.

properties.name: RyÅ«jin
properties.description: Dragon King of the Sea. Lives in a coral palace (RyÅ«gÅ«-jÅ) at the bottom of the ocean. Controls tides with magical jewels. Ancestor of the imperial line.

properties.name: Chaac
properties.description: Maya rain god with a lightning axe. Four Chaacs govern the four directions. His long nose represents rain clouds. Essential for maize agriculture.

properties.name: Ah Puch
properties.description: Skeletal Maya death god who ruled Mitnal (ninth level of Xibalba). Wore bells, owl feathers, and rotting flesh. Associated with war and sacrifice.

properties.name: Supay
properties.description: Inca god of the underworld. After Spanish colonization, syncretized with the Devil. Mining communities offer sacrifices (tinka) to Supay for safety underground.

properties.name: Coatlicue
properties.description: Earth mother with a skirt of serpents and a necklace of hearts, hands, and skulls. Mother of Huitzilopochtli. Both creator and devourer.

properties.name: Xipe Totec
properties.description: Aztec god of spring and renewal who wore flayed human skin representing new vegetation covering the earth. Patron of goldsmiths.

properties.name: Dazhbog
properties.description: Slavic sun god, son of Svarog the sky-smith. Giver of wealth and abundance. Ancestor of all Slavic people according to the Tale of Igor's Campaign.

properties.name: Stribog
properties.description: Slavic god of wind, air, and storms. Grandfather of the winds. Winds were called his grandchildren in the Tale of Igor's Campaign.

properties.name: Rod
properties.description: Supreme creator god of Slavic religion. Broke the cosmic egg to create the universe. Father of all beings and cosmic order.

properties.name: Maitreya
properties.description: The future Buddha who will appear when dharma has been forgotten. Currently resides in Tushita heaven. Represents eternal hope for renewal.

properties.name: Green Tara
properties.description: Female bodhisattva of swift compassionate action. Born from Avalokiteshvara's tears. Her right foot is extended, ready to spring into action to help.

properties.name: Yamantaka
properties.description: Wrathful form of Manjushri who conquered the death god Yama. Bull-headed with multiple faces and arms. Represents wisdom conquering death itself.

properties.name: Erlik Khan
properties.description: Ruler of the Mongolian underworld. Judge of the dead. First being created who fell to evil. Shamans negotiate with him for souls of the sick.

properties.name: Astghik
properties.description: Armenian goddess of love, beauty, and water. Beloved of Vahagn. Her festival Vardavar (Rose Festival) involved water-splashing. Still celebrated today.

properties.name: Dali
properties.description: Georgian goddess of the hunt and mountains. Beautiful golden-haired deity who protects wild animals. Punishes hunters who kill without need.

properties.name: Eros
properties.description: God of desire and erotic love. In early tradition, a primordial force that emerged from Chaos. Later depicted as Aphrodite's mischievous son with bow and arrows.

properties.name: Nike
properties.description: Winged goddess of victory. Companion of Athena and Zeus. Inspired the famous statue Winged Victory of Samothrace and the modern brand.

properties.name: Kronos
properties.description: Titan king who devoured his children to prevent prophecy. Zeus escaped and overthrew him. In Roman tradition (as Saturn), ruled a lost Golden Age.

properties.name: Saturn
properties.description: Ancient Roman god of time and agriculture. Ruled during the mythical Golden Age. The wild Saturnalia festival honored him each December.

properties.name: Bacchus
properties.description: Roman god of wine and ecstatic freedom. His cult (Bacchanalia) became so wild the Roman Senate banned it in 186 BCE.

properties.name: Nephthys
properties.description: Goddess of death and mourning. Sister of Isis, Osiris, and Set. Protector of the dead. Together with Isis, she mourned Osiris and guided souls.

properties.name: Khepri
properties.description: Scarab-headed god of the dawn and self-creation. Pushed the sun across the sky like a dung beetle rolls its ball. Embodiment of daily renewal.

properties.name: Anu
properties.description: Sky father and supreme authority among the Mesopotamian gods. Father of Enlil. His throne was the heavens. Distant and rarely intervened directly.

properties.name: Kama
properties.description: God of love and desire. Shoots flower arrows from a sugarcane bow. Burned to ash by Shiva's third eye but later reborn as Krishna's son Pradyumna.

properties.name: Amesemi
properties.description: Consort of Apedemak and protector of Kushite royalty. Depicted with falcon headdress. One of the few uniquely Nubian goddesses without Egyptian origin.

properties.name: Ungnyeo
properties.description: The she-bear who became human after 100 days of eating garlic and mugwort in a cave. Mother of Dangun, founder of Korea. Represents patience and endurance.

properties.name: San-shin
properties.description: Korean Mountain God, one of the most widely worshipped deities. Each mountain has its own San-shin. Often depicted with a tiger. Shrines exist at most Buddhist temples.

properties.name: TÅ«
properties.description: Polynesian god of war and hunting. Only sibling who wanted to fight Rangi and Papa to separate them. Patron of warriors and fishermen.
